hints.tr: `urlencode(forecast_params)` yalnızca `city=...&units=...` kısmını verir; başına `forecast_base + "?"` eklemek sana kalıyor.
hints.en: `urlencode(forecast_params)` gives only the `city=...&units=...` part; adding `forecast_base + "?"` in front is up to you.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
from urllib.parse import urlencode

forecast_base = "https://api.example.com/v1/forecast"
forecast_params = {"city": "New York", "units": "metric", "days": 3}

search_base = "https://api.example.com/v1/search"

url = forecast_base + "?" + urlencode(forecast_params)
search_url = search_base + "?" + urlencode({"q": "fish & chips", "lang": "en"})

print(url)
print(search_url)
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
from urllib.parse import urlencode

forecast_base = "https://api.example.com/v1/forecast"
forecast_params = {"city": "New York", "units": "metric", "days": 3}

search_base = "https://api.example.com/v1/search"

url = forecast_base + "?" + urlencode(forecast_params)
search_url = search_base + "?" + urlencode({"q": "fish & chips", "lang": "en"})

print(url)
print(search_url)
```
